title: Conditional logistic regression for a matched case-control study
summary: Estimates the exposure odds ratio conditional on the matched sets, eliminating the matching factor from the likelihood rather than adjusting for it.
_keying: Keyed on the TYPED ESTIMAND and the method, never on what generated code calls itself. Measured 2026-09-06: 26 R blocks in the corpus carried 26 distinct analysis headers with zero repeats, because a header is a study-specific description. Roughly 18 methods sit behind those 26 blocks.

sizing._why: A matched or nested case-control has no closed-form sample-size formula among the standard two-group ones and must not borrow one: the paired formula is for a continuous mean difference. The honest route is the discordant-set method (Dupont 1988); epiR::epi.sscc implements it in R.

pinned_defaults: R: method = 'exact'. clogit passes through to coxph, whose default is ties = 'efron'; the two differ when a matched set holds more than one case.
R: exposure kept numeric 0/1, so no alphabetical factor ordering can silently choose the reference level and invert the odds ratio.
Python: no intercept. A conditional likelihood has none, so the design matrix is built explicitly rather than from a formula string that would add one.
